sentences.text: 4. The informant lady aged 21 years has lodged a report on 08.07.2022, on the basis of which crime has been registered.
The Police have carried investigation and on completion filed final report.
It is informant's case that she was well acquainted with applicant- Sarang since the year 2017.
Their casual acquaintance turned into love affair.
All the time they were meeting with each other at different places.
The applicant expressed his desire to marry but on informant attaining majority.
It is her contention that during the year 2017 to 2018 they had physical relationship.

In the year 2019,
the informant attained majority and expressed to marry but she learnt that applicant is a married fellow.
Despite his marriage, the applicant assured that he would leave his wife and would marry with her.
Thereafter, the relations continued for next 2 to 3 years.
Finally on 16 th June, 2022, the applicant beated the informant, therefore, she lodged the report.
5. The applicant's learned counsel would submit that it is a case of consensual relationship.
It is specifically argued that though the parties were acquainted with each other since the year 2017, but they had physically relations after informant attaining majority.

Moreover, it is submitted that the offence under the Special Act would not attract since there was no intention on the part of applicant to commit an offence only for the reason that the informant belongs to the member of Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribes.
In order to substantiate said contention applicant's learned counsel has attracted our attention to an agreement dated 14th March, 2022 entered in between the parties.

Apart from settlement, this document is pressed into service to falsify the contention of the F.I.R.
that in the year 2017 and 2018 they had physical relationship.

We have been taken through the document wherein the informant herself has stated on 14.3.2022 that, the physical relationship was from last one year meaning thereby they had physical contact after the informant attained majority.
This document is not denied by the informant.
6. Moreover, the informant lady has appeared and filed affidavit stating that out of misunderstanding she has lodged the report.
The matter is settled and she do not wish to go on with the prosecution.
Moreover, she has stated that six other criminal cases have been filed by the applicant and his wife against her which are also settled and the applicant has agreed for withdrawal those cases.
7. Apart from the settlement it reveals that there are no allegations of use of force or compulsion, it is case of love relationship.
The only aspect is whether during minority the parties had sexual relations.
Though the informant has vaguely stated that they had relationship in past, however, she did not specified the details in any manner.
On the other hand, her affidavit speaks that during last one year from entering into agreement dated 14.3.2022 they had physical relations.
Thus, it is Sarang S/O Keshavrao Admane vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Gadge Nagar ...

2 difficult to accede the vague statement that the parties had relationship in past.
Moreover, the matter has been amicably settled.
Pertinent to note that six other criminal cases are pending between the parties which are also settled and would be disposed, as a result of settlement arrived in all the matters.
It is informed that yet the charges have not been framed.
The informant lady is of marriageable age and thus it is submitted that pending several prosecutions would come in her marital prospects.

8. The applicant's learned counsel relied on the decisions of this Court in the case of Sonu @ Dilip Vitthalrao Gawande and another Vs. State of Maharashtra, through Police Station Officer, P.S.
Akola, Civil Lines, Akola, Tq. and District Akola and another, delivered in Criminal Application (APL) No.1041 of 2023 dated 1st November, 2023, to contend that there is no embargo in quashing the proceeding arising out of a special statute.

sentences.text: True, the powers under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code are unlimited, which are only guided by the principle of preventing abuse of the process of the Court or to secure the ends of justice.
The contents of F.I.R. coupled with material collected during the course of investigation makes out a case of consensual relations between two adults.
Prima facie it is evident that physical relationship was after the informant attaining majority meaning thereby the provisions of Special Act may not attract.
Besides that, the parties have settled the matter.
There is no material to infer that the act was committed only on the ground that victim was member of Scheduled caste or Scheduled tribe.
Thus, it is evident that no case is made out for continuation of prosecution.
The applicant's learned counsel would submit that the applicant would deposit sum of Rs.50,000/- for rotating the police machinery.
9. In the circumstances, the application is allowed.

10. We hereby quash and set aside the criminal prosecution bearing Special Case No.288/2022 pending on the file of District and Sessions Judge, Amravati arising out of Crime No.770/2022,
registered with Police Station Gadge Nagar, District Amravati, for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 506(2), 504, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4, 8, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(1)(w)
(i), 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) and 3(2)(7) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
11.
